sender.en: “Customer Care” or “Loan” page using your bank’s name on X, Facebook or Telegram

name.en: Fake bank customer care or loan page on social media

how.en: When you complain about a failed transfer or debit on your bank’s X or Facebook page, a lookalike account quickly replies as “customer care” and moves you to WhatsApp. It sends a form asking for your account number, card details and PIN, then asks for the OTPs that arrive, and empties the account. Other fake pages using a bank’s name and logo offer quick loans that need an upfront fee or your card details. Wema Bank found more than 70 fake accounts on X in 2026.

text.en: After you post a complaint, an account using the bank’s name replies and offers help.
It moves you to WhatsApp or a form link.
The form asks for your card number, PIN and the OTPs you receive.
Or a page offers a quick loan if you pay a fee first.
Hello, we are sorry about your failed transfer. Kindly reach our live resolution desk on WhatsApp via [link] and fill the reversal form so your funds can be returned within 10 minutes.

A “customer care” account that replies to your public complaint and moves you to WhatsApp.
Forms asking for card numbers, PINs or OTPs.
Loan pages that want a fee or your card details first.
Contact your bank only through its app, the number on your card or a branch, not through replies on social media.
Never type your PIN or share an OTP with anyone.
If you shared details, call your bank at once, and report the page to the platform and the NPF-NCCC.
